title: The Group Chat of Route 9
premise: August Almeida has spent four years at Route 9 High perfecting the art of being unseen—until his civics teacher pairs him with Priya Chandrasekaran, the student body president who once got him suspended, to document the town's fading Harvest Bread Festival for a semester project. Digging through the festival's archives, August and Priya uncover that the beloved tradition was built on a land deal that swindled August's great-grandfather, and that the town council—led by Priya's mother—has been quietly selling the festival grounds to a developer. Torn between loyalty to family, to each other, and to the truth, the pair must decide whether exposing the corruption will save the festival or destroy it, culminating in a graduation-eve bake-off where August bakes the evidence into a hundred loaves of bread and the town must choose its memory over its myth.
about_author: Ines Montrose grew up above her family's bakery in a small river town, where she learned that every recipe hides a history. She writes young adult stories about kids who discover that their hometowns are more complicated—and more worth fighting for—than they ever imagined.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: August's POV. On the first day of senior year, August bakes his anxiety into a batch of sourdough and navigates the halls of Route 9 High with surgical invisibility. A flashback to last spring's suspension shows why Priya Chandrasekaran is his nemesis. Emotional beat: the exhausting cost of staying small.

chapters.title: The Pairing
chapters.summary: August's POV. Civics teacher Mr. Okafor announces the semester-long Legacy Project and reads the pairs aloud: Almeida and Chandrasekaran, assigned to document the Harvest Bread Festival. Priya is thrilled; August is furious. Their first planning meeting collapses into recriminations. Emotional beat: resentment with a crack of reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Flour and Ash
chapters.summary: August's POV. August gives Priya a grudging tour of his father's bakery, showing her how he bakes feelings into bread—grief rye, apology brioche. Priya admits she doesn't actually love student government; she loves her mother's approval. Emotional beat: two enemies discovering they're both performing.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Researching at the historical society, Priya finds the festival's founding ledger and a name that stops her cold: Almeida. She pockets a photograph of August's great-grandfather standing in front of the original festival ovens. Emotional beat: the first pull of a mystery bigger than a grade.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: August's POV. August and Priya sign an uneasy truce—she handles interviews, he handles the baking history. At a council meeting they watch Priya's mother, Councilwoman Chandrasekaran, deflect questions about the festival grounds' maintenance. Emotional beat: the dawning sense that adults are hiding something.

chapters.title: Great-Grandpa's Ledger
chapters.summary: August's POV. August's grandmother, Nonna Rosa, shows him the family's copy of the 1952 land agreement: the Almeidas donated the festival grounds in exchange for a permanent booth and a promise the land would never be sold. The council's copy says otherwise. Emotional beat: betrayal that tastes like family.

chapters.title: The Forged Page
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya compares the ledgers and confirms the council's version is a forgery—her mother's signature style, her mother's era. She says nothing to August and starts pulling files alone at night. Emotional beat: the first lie of omission, heavy as wet dough.

chapters.title: Detention, Together
chapters.summary: August's POV. Caught sneaking into the records annex after hours, August and Priya land in detention, where they finally trade theories instead of insults. August realizes Priya has been holding back. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in punishment, shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: Developer's Delight
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya discovers the Meridian Group's proposal: a retail complex on the festival grounds, fast-tracked with council votes bought through quiet favors—including her mother's campaign donors. Emotional beat: horror at realizing the corruption has a face she loves.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya's mother finds her research and issues an ultimatum: drop the project's historical angle or lose her blessing, her college fund, and the family's name. Priya agrees out loud—and keeps a copy of everything. Emotional beat: love against duty, duty winning in public.

chapters.title: The Midterm Presentation
chapters.summary: August's POV. August and Priya present a sanitized version of the festival's history to the class; Mr. Okafor gives it an A but privately asks August why the story feels hollow. August confronts Priya about what she's hiding. Emotional beat: success that tastes like failure.

chapters.title: Bread for an Apology
chapters.summary: August's POV. August bakes a reconciliation loaf—fig and rosemary—and leaves it on Priya's porch with the forged ledger page. Priya comes to the bakery at closing and shows him the Meridian file. Emotional beat: the truce becomes an alliance, and something warmer.

chapters.title: The Almeida Booth
chapters.summary: August's POV. The council votes to revoke the Almeida family's festival booth, citing safety codes—retaliation for August's records requests. Nonna Rosa, dignified in the council chamber, tells the story of 1952 aloud for the first time in decades. Emotional beat: public grief, quiet fury.

chapters.title: Allies in Odd Places
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya recruits the school paper's editor, a retired archivist, and Mr. Okafor, who reveals the Legacy Project was designed to make students interrogate the town's myths. August hesitates—exposure could get his family's bakery blacklisted. Emotional beat: the cost of truth made concrete.

chapters.title: Leaked
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The school paper publishes the forged ledger and Meridian proposal; the town erupts. Priya's mother suspends the festival 'pending review,' blaming the students for poisoning the well. August and Priya's friendship fractures under the fallout. Emotional beat: victory that feels like arson.

chapters.title: The Empty Oven
chapters.summary: August's POV. August's father, terrified of losing the bakery's supplier contracts, forbids August from continuing. August, who has spent his whole life obeying, bakes alone at midnight and realizes silence is the one ingredient he refuses to use. Emotional beat: a son outgrowing his father's fear.

chapters.title: What Priya Kept
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya finds her mother's private correspondence proving she forged the ledger to protect her own father's reputation—not for greed, but for love twisted into cover-up. Priya must decide whether mercy and justice can share a page. Emotional beat: compassion complicating conviction.

chapters.title: The Bake-Off Clause
chapters.summary: August's POV. August discovers in the original 1952 charter that the festival cannot be cancelled while the Almeida family's ovens stand—so the council moves to demolish them before graduation. The students have one week. Emotional beat: the ticking clock, flour-dusted and desperate.

chapters.title: A Hundred Loaves
chapters.summary: August's POV. Graduation eve: August and Priya organize a defiant community bake-off in the old ovens. August bakes the evidence into a hundred loaves—each loaf's paper insert telling one chapter of the real 1952 story—and the town lines up to read. Emotional beat: truth served warm, one household at a time.

chapters.title: Councilwoman Chandrasekaran
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. With the town holding the loaves and the story, Priya publicly confronts her mother at the emergency council session, offering the mercy of context alongside the demand for resignation. Her mother steps down; the demolition order dies. Emotional beat: love and duty finally on the same side.

chapters.title: The Festival of Route 9
chapters.summary: August's POV. The Harvest Bread Festival returns, restored to the charter, with the Almeida booth at its center and Nonna Rosa cutting the first loaf. August and Priya, standing in the crowd they built, finally kiss among the flour dust. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not inherited.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: August's POV. At graduation, August and Priya turn in the Legacy Project—the real one. Mr. Okafor reads its last line aloud: 'A town is a recipe; someone always wrote it down first.' August, no longer invisible, walks the stage with his head up. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
